```{=html}
<h2 class="lx-sr">Task</h2>
<div class="lx-card ckr-intro">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">How this checkpoint works · about 240 minutes, no hints</p>
<ol class="ckr-parts">
<li><b>A · A stranger's study</b> (about 45 min). Review the co-op proposal below with the review form and submit it as task 1; the seven marked tasks (2–5, 9–11) open after it.</li>
<li><b>B · Your mock review</b> (about 60 min). Get a written review of your <a href="cr-your-own-study.html">research capstone</a>'s question and method: from a mentor, a peer, or yourself after a day away.</li>
<li><b>C · Respond and revise</b> (about 70 min). Answer each concern point by point; revise your proposal and log each change.</li>
<li><b>D · Rerun</b> (about 50 min). Order and check the co-op study's rerun (tasks 9 to 11), then rerun your own main result from a <span class="lx-term" data-term="clean-clone">clean clone</span>.</li>
<li><b>Submit</b> (about 15 min). Enter your results in the twelve tasks below, in any order. The worked review, response and revision open once all twelve are answered.</li>
</ol>
<p class="lx-hint">When to take it: once your research capstone has a proposal and a main result. A review from someone else can take days: ask for it first, and do part A while you wait.</p>
<p class="lx-eyebrow">How it is marked, before you start</p>
<ul class="ckr-rules">
<li><b>Proficient:</b> at least 5 of the 7 auto-marked tasks right on the first try, plus at least 3 of the 4 points of each written task (1, 6, 7, 8 and 12).</li>
<li><b>Strong:</b> at least 6 of 7 on the first try, and every written point.</li>
<li><b>Opening solutions early:</b> a task whose answer you open first counts as not right (a written task: no points). Opening the worked solution before all twelve are answered makes the attempt practice, with no level.</li>
<li><b>After the worked solution opens:</b> an answer given after that counts as practice, not as right, and a written task then earns no points.</li>
<li><b>Task 1 first:</b> the seven marked tasks open once your review is submitted. Each written task stays as you submit it. A review submitted after a marked task was answered earns no points.</li>
<li><b>The level is not the table's:</b> it comes from this rule. The criterion table in the rubric section rates the work itself; its Strong asks for a review and a rerun by someone else.</li>
</ul>
<p class="lx-hint">Refreshers: <a href="r01-framing.html">R1</a> (framing), <a href="r03-system-and-method.html">R3</a> (method), <a href="r05-build-validate.html">R5</a> (reruns), <a href="r08-communicating.html">R8</a> (findings with limits), <a href="r09-integrity-stakeholders.html">R9</a> (integrity), <a href="r10-question-studio.html">R10</a> (the question card), <a href="m14-did-it-work.html">M14</a> (difference-in-differences), <a href="k08-git-notebooks.html">K8</a> (clones).</p>
<p class="lx-hint"><b>Words in the tasks:</b> <span class="lx-term" data-term="co-op">co-op</span> (an electric cooperative), <span class="lx-term" data-term="repository">repository</span>, <span class="lx-term" data-term="clean-clone">clean clone</span>, <span class="lx-term" data-term="linear-regression">regression</span> and <span class="lx-term" data-term="agent-based-model">agent-based model</span>. Tap one for its meaning.</p>
</div>

<div class="lx-row2 ckr-a">
<div class="lx-card ckr-study" id="ckr-study">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Part A · the proposal to review</p>
<!-- ckr-study:start (written from the data file by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<h3>Did a night-pumping tariff move irrigation out of the co-op's peak?</h3>
<p>A graduate student's proposal, with a first result, for the board of Prairie Valley Co-op.</p>
<dl class="ckr-fields"><div><dt>Question</dt><dd>Did Prairie Valley Co-op's 2024 night-pumping tariff lower irrigation peak demand?</dd></div><div><dt>Type</dt><dd>Evaluative.</dd></div><div><dt>Audience</dt><dd>The co-op's board, which votes in 2026 on keeping the tariff.</dd></div><div><dt>Billing</dt><dd>The co-op's wholesale bill charges for its load in its 20 highest-load summer hours.</dd></div><div><dt>The tariff</dt><dd>Cheaper energy from 22:00 to 06:00 and a higher price from 14:00 to 20:00 on summer weekdays. Each farm chose whether to join.</dd></div><div><dt>Data</dt><dd>Hourly meter readings of the co-op's 112 irrigation pumps, summers 2020 to 2024.</dd></div><div><dt>Metric</dt><dd>Peak demand, kW per pump.</dd></div><div><dt>Method</dt><dd><span class="lx-term" data-term="difference-in-differences">Difference-in-differences</span>: the 41 pumps that joined in 2024 against the 71 that did not, before and after.</dd></div><div><dt>Literature</dt><dd>Five studies of <span class="lx-term" data-term="time-of-use-tariff">time-of-use tariffs</span> for households.</dd></div><div><dt>Checks</dt><dd>Run once, on data the author cleaned by hand in a spreadsheet.</dd></div><div><dt>First result</dt><dd>Peak demand fell 6.2 kW per pump.</dd></div></dl>
<p class="lx-hint">The co-op, its farms and every number here are fictional: the results are assumed example outputs, not computed from data.</p>
<!-- ckr-study:end -->
</div>
<div class="lx-card ckr-forms">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">The forms</p>
<p class="ckr-lede">Four plain templates: one for a review, one for a response, a change log and a rerun report. Use them for the co-op proposal and for your own study.</p>
<!-- ckr-forms:start (written from the data file by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<details class="lx-textalt ckr-form" data-form="review"><summary>The review form (parts A and B)</summary><pre>1. The study in one or two sentences: question, method, data.
2. The main claim it will make, and the evidence it plans.
3. Major concerns (at most three): ones that could change the conclusion. For each: the rubric competence, and what evidence or change would answer it.
4. Minor concerns.
5. One alternative method from another family, and what it would show that this one cannot.
6. Can the main result be rerun from the repository? What is missing?
7. Recommendation: proceed; proceed once the major concerns are answered; or rethink the question.</pre></details>
<details class="lx-textalt ckr-form" data-form="response"><summary>The response (part C)</summary><pre>For each concern, in the reviewer's order:
Concern 1 (competence): accepted / partly accepted / declined.
Reason: one or two sentences.
Change: what changed, and where (a section of the proposal, a file in the repository).
Evidence: a test, a figure or a number, where you have one.</pre></details>
<details class="lx-textalt ckr-form" data-form="log"><summary>The change log (part C)</summary><pre>One line per change:
Before → after · the concern it answers · where.
Then: your rubric self-rating after the revision, competence by competence, and any level that moved, with its evidence.</pre></details>
<details class="lx-textalt ckr-form" data-form="rerun"><summary>The rerun report (part D)</summary><pre>Repository and commit; date; machine and environment.
Tolerance for the main result, written down before the rerun.
Reported value; rerun value; difference as a share of the reported value (in the result's units if that value is near zero).
Qualitative work: the audit trail followed from the raw material, each theme traced to its sources, coding decisions and discrepancies explained.
Cause of any difference, and the fix in the repository.
Who reran it (you, or someone else).</pre></details>
<!-- ckr-forms:end -->
<p class="lx-hint">Words used in the tasks and forms: <span class="lx-term" data-term="clean-clone">clean clone</span>, <span class="lx-term" data-term="lock-file">lock file</span>, <span class="lx-term" data-term="checksum">checksum</span>, <span class="lx-term" data-term="confidence-interval">95% interval</span>, <span class="lx-term" data-term="commit">commit</span>, <span class="lx-term" data-term="software-environment">environment</span>, <span class="lx-term" data-term="audit-trail">audit trail</span>, <span class="lx-term" data-term="matched-comparison">matched comparison</span>.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">Reviewing a peer's proposal: keep it confidential and do not use its ideas without permission (ALLEA 2023, §2.8). Reviewing your own: wait a day, and read it as someone who has not seen it.</p>
</div>
</div>

<div class="lx-interactive" data-learn="ck-r-defend-revise" data-src="../assets/learn/data/ck-r-defend-revise.json">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<!-- ckr-tasks:start (written from the data file by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<p class="lx-hint"><b>Without JavaScript:</b> nothing here is locked or marked, and the worked solution is further down the page, so use this list as practice. A level needs the interactive tasks.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">Write task 1, your review, before you open the marked tasks: their questions name concerns your review should find.</p>
<ol class="ckr-static">
<li><p><b>Your review of the co-op proposal</b> <span class="lx-hint">Part A · Write a review</span></p><p>Review the co-op proposal above with the review form: the study in one or two sentences, at most three major concerns, the minor ones, and what would answer each. Paste your review.</p><p>Self-rated against 4 points, shown after you submit.</p></li>
<li><p><b>Opens after task 1</b> <span class="lx-hint">Part A</span></p><details class="ckr-later"><summary>Open after task 1, your review</summary><p><b>The most serious concern</b> <span class="lx-hint">Rank the concerns</span></p><p>Which concern could most change the study's conclusion?</p><ul><li>a. Only five studies are cited, all of households, so the map of what is known is thin.</li><li>b. Each farm chose whether to join, so the joiners may differ from the rest in ways that also change their pumping.</li><li>c. The proposal does not name the software, or its version, that ran the regression.</li><li>d. The board votes on the tariff in 2026, which leaves the study little time to finish.</li></ul></details></li>
<li><p><b>Opens after task 1</b> <span class="lx-hint">Part A</span></p><details class="ckr-later"><summary>Open after task 1, your review</summary><p><b>Whose peak?</b> <span class="lx-hint">Name the competence</span></p><p>A reviewer writes: “The proposal never says whose peak: each pump's own highest hour, or the co-op's highest-load hours.” Which rubric competence does this concern?</p><ul><li>a. Framing</li><li>b. Positioning</li><li>c. Integrity</li><li>d. Communication</li></ul></details></li>
<li><p><b>Opens after task 1</b> <span class="lx-hint">Part A</span></p><details class="ckr-later"><summary>Open after task 1, your review</summary><p><b>Answering the selection concern</b> <span class="lx-hint">Answer a critique</span></p><p>The authors answer the selection concern. Which response answers it, rather than deflecting it?</p><ul><li>a. Self-selection affects most observational studies, so we list it as an accepted limitation in section 6.</li><li>b. We will add more pumps from this summer to the sample, so that the estimate is more precise.</li><li>c. We now compare the 2024 joiners with the 29 farms that joined in 2025, before they joined, and show both groups' four summers before the tariff.</li><li>d. The reviewer has misunderstood the tariff: farms join it for reasons that have nothing to do with pumping.</li></ul></details></li>
<li><p><b>Opens after task 1</b> <span class="lx-hint">Part A</span></p><details class="ckr-later"><summary>Open after task 1, your review</summary><p><b>From Proficient to Strong</b> <span class="lx-hint">Move a competence up a level</span></p><p>The revised study is Proficient on Method fit: difference-in-differences, defended against a matched comparison and a pump-scheduling simulation. Which change moves it to Strong?</p><ul><li>a. Add a third alternative method, an agent-based model of the farmers, to the methods compared.</li><li>b. State the method's main limit here (the later joiners' demand might still have moved differently) and partly mitigate it: show that both groups' peak-hour demand moved together in the four summers before 2024.</li><li>c. Replace difference-in-differences with a machine-learning model trained on every pump's hourly readings.</li><li>d. Write a longer method section that explains difference-in-differences step by step.</li></ul></details></li>
<li><p><b>Your mock review</b> <span class="lx-hint">Part B · Get a review</span></p><p>Get a written review of your research capstone's question and method (the review form; a mentor, a peer, or you after a day away). Paste it, and say who wrote it.</p><p>Self-rated against 4 points, shown after you submit.</p></li>
<li><p><b>Your response</b> <span class="lx-hint">Part C · Answer the critique</span></p><p>Answer each major concern point by point: accepted, partly accepted or declined, with a reason, and for each accepted one the change and where it is made. Paste your response.</p><p>Self-rated against 4 points, shown after you submit.</p></li>
<li><p><b>Your revision</b> <span class="lx-hint">Part C · Revise and log</span></p><p>Revise your proposal. Paste your change log (before → after, and the concern each change answers) and your rubric self-rating after the revision.</p><p>Self-rated against 4 points, shown after you submit.</p></li>
<li><p><b>Opens after task 1</b> <span class="lx-hint">Part D</span></p><details class="ckr-later"><summary>Open after task 1, your review</summary><p><b>A clean-clone rerun</b> <span class="lx-hint">Rerun from a clean clone</span></p><p>After the review, the authors rerun the revised co-op study from a clean clone. Each step needs the one before it. Put the steps in order.</p><ul><li>Compare the main result with the reported value, against the tolerance written down beforehand.</li><li>Build the environment from the repository's lock file.</li><li>Run the whole pipeline, from raw data to the main result, with one command.</li><li>Clone the repository into a new, empty folder.</li><li>Log the outcome, and any difference with its cause, in the verification log.</li><li>Fetch the raw data with the repository's script, which runs in that environment, and check the checksums.</li></ul><p>Put these in order.</p></details></li>
<li><p><b>Opens after task 1</b> <span class="lx-hint">Part D</span></p><details class="ckr-later"><summary>Open after task 1, your review</summary><p><b>How far apart?</b> <span class="lx-hint">Report a difference</span></p><p>Reported: a fall of 4.6 kW per pump. The clean-clone rerun: 4.3 kW. How far apart are they, as a share of the reported value?</p><p class="lx-hint">Within 2% of the value (about 0.13 percentage points) counts as right.</p><p>Answer with a number and a unit.</p></details></li>
<li><p><b>Opens after task 1</b> <span class="lx-hint">Part D</span></p><details class="ckr-later"><summary>Open after task 1, your review</summary><p><b>What to report</b> <span class="lx-hint">Report it honestly</span></p><p>The tolerance written down before the rerun was 1%. What should the authors do?</p><ul><li>a. Report 4.6 kW, the published value: a gap of 0.3 kW is small next to the interval.</li><li>b. Report 4.3 kW instead, since the clean clone is the run to trust, and drop 4.6.</li><li>c. Find the cause, turn any hand step into code with a stated rule, rerun from a clean clone, and log both numbers, the cause and the fix.</li><li>d. Widen the tolerance to 10%, since 1% was too strict for real meter data.</li></ul></details></li>
<li><p><b>Your rerun</b> <span class="lx-hint">Part D · Rerun your own result</span></p><p>Rerun your own main result from a clean clone, or follow your audit trail for qualitative work. Paste your rerun report (the form above).</p><p>Self-rated against 4 points, shown after you submit.</p></li>
</ol>
<!-- ckr-tasks:end -->
</div>
</div>
```

## Worked solution
:::

```{=html}
<div id="ckr-lock" class="lx-ck-lock" hidden>
<p><b>Opens once all twelve tasks are answered.</b> Your own review, response, revision and rerun come first, so the worked examples wait. Opening them now makes this attempt practice, with no level.</p>
<p><button type="button" class="lx-btn ghost small">Open them anyway (recorded: practice)</button></p>
</div>
<div id="ckr-solution-body" class="lx-xgrid lx-ck-gated ckr-solution-body">
<!-- ckr-solution:start (written from the data file by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<div class="lx-xcard ckr-ex" id="ckr-ex-review"><header class="lx-x-head"><h3>Two reviews of the co-op proposal</h3></header><p class="lx-hint">Review the co-op proposal: the study, the major and minor concerns, and what would answer each.</p>
<div class="lx-ex-cols">
<div class="lx-ex-ans weak"><p class="lx-eyebrow">A weak review · Developing</p><p class="lx-ex-lines"><b>Summary:</b> An interesting study of a new tariff.
<b>Concerns:</b> The literature review is thin. [1] The method seems fine. [2] Figure 2 is hard to read. [3]
<b>Recommendation:</b> accept with minor changes. [4]</p><ol class="lx-ex-static"><li value="1"><b>Falls short:</b> A minor concern led with as if it were the main one; no competence named, and nothing that would answer it.</li><li value="2"><b>Falls short:</b> Each farm chose whether to join: the comparison is untested.</li><li value="3"><b>Falls short:</b> Format, not substance: it cannot change the conclusion.</li><li value="4"><b>Falls short:</b> A verdict without reasons the authors can act on.</li></ol></div>
<div class="lx-ex-ans good"><p class="lx-eyebrow">The worked review · Strong</p><p class="lx-ex-lines"><b>Summary:</b> asks whether the 2024 tariff lowered the pumps' peak demand, by difference-in-differences on 112 pumps' meter readings, 2020 to 2024. [1]
<b>Major 1 · Method fit:</b> farms chose whether to join, so their demand may have moved differently even without the tariff; show the summers before, and try farms that joined later as a comparison. [2]
<b>Major 2 · Framing:</b> say whose peak, in kW, over which hours: the co-op is billed for its 20 highest-load summer hours, not for each pump's own peak. [3]
<b>Major 3 · Trustworthy analysis:</b> the hand cleaning in a spreadsheet is not documented, and the proposal does not supply what a rerun from the raw data needs. [4]
<b>Minor · Positioning:</b> the five studies are of households; add studies of farm or business tariffs. [5]
<b>Another family:</b> a pump-scheduling simulation would show how much pumping could move at most, which meter data cannot. [6]
<b>Recommendation:</b> proceed once the three major concerns are answered. [7]</p><ol class="lx-ex-static"><li value="1"><b>Works:</b> The study stated fairly, before any criticism.</li><li value="2"><b>Works:</b> The concern that could change the conclusion comes first, with the evidence that would answer it.</li><li value="3"><b>Works:</b> Tied to a competence, and to what the decision-maker needs.</li><li value="4"><b>Works:</b> Parts can still be checked independently; a full rerun from the raw data is not yet possible.</li><li value="5"><b>Works:</b> Kept minor: it could sharpen the method, but threatens the conclusion less than selection.</li><li value="6"><b>Works:</b> An alternative from another method family, and what it adds.</li><li value="7"><b>Works:</b> A verdict tied to the concerns.</li></ol></div>
</div>
<table class="lx-facts lx-ex-diff"><thead><tr><th scope="col"></th><th scope="col">A weak review</th><th scope="col">The worked review</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Order</th><td>A minor concern first</td><td>By what could change the conclusion</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Competences</th><td>None named</td><td>One for each concern</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">What would answer it</th><td>Not said</td><td>Said for each major concern</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Another family</th><td>None</td><td>A simulation, and what it adds</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p class="lx-hint">Both reviews are illustrative; the study is fictional.</p></div>
<div class="lx-xcard ckr-ex" id="ckr-ex-response"><header class="lx-x-head"><h3>Two answers to Major 1</h3></header><p class="lx-hint">Answer the concern that the farms chose whether to join.</p>
<div class="lx-ex-cols">
<div class="lx-ex-ans weak"><p class="lx-eyebrow">A deflecting answer · Developing</p><p class="lx-ex-lines"><b>Response:</b> We thank the reviewer. Self-selection is a well-known limitation of observational studies, [1] and we have added it to the limitations section. [2]</p><ol class="lx-ex-static"><li value="1"><b>Falls short:</b> It names the problem and keeps it.</li><li value="2"><b>Falls short:</b> A sentence moved; the analysis unchanged.</li></ol></div>
<div class="lx-ex-ans good"><p class="lx-eyebrow">An answering response · Strong</p><p class="lx-ex-lines">Accepted, with thanks to the reviewer.
<b>Change:</b> the comparison group is now the 29 farms that joined in 2025, before they joined (section 3; analysis/did.py). [1]
<b>Evidence:</b> in the four summers before 2024, the two groups' peak-hour demand moved within 0.5 kW of each other each year (Figure 2). [2]
<b>Result:</b> with this comparison and the metric of Major 2, the fall is 4.6 kW per pump, not 6.2. [3]
<b>Limit kept:</b> the later joiners' demand might still have moved differently; stated in section 6. [4]</p><ol class="lx-ex-static"><li value="1"><b>Works:</b> The change, and where it is made.</li><li value="2"><b>Works:</b> New evidence for the <span class="lx-term" data-term="parallel-trends">parallel-trends</span> assumption.</li><li value="3"><b>Works:</b> The change moved the answer, and the response says so.</li><li value="4"><b>Works:</b> What the change cannot fix, said plainly.</li></ol></div>
</div>
<p class="lx-hint">Both answers are illustrative.</p></div>
<div class="lx-xcard ckr-ex" id="ckr-ex-revision"><header class="lx-x-head"><h3>The revision: what moved it from Proficient to Strong</h3></header><p class="lx-hint">The revised study's question, method, checks and result.</p>
<div class="lx-ex-cols">
<div class="lx-ex-ans prof"><p class="lx-eyebrow">Revised: Proficient · Proficient</p><p class="lx-ex-lines"><b>Question:</b> Did the 2024 tariff lower the joining pumps' average demand, in kW per pump, in the co-op's 20 billing hours, compared with farms that joined in 2025, before they joined? [1]
<b>Would count against it:</b> no larger fall among the joiners than among the 2025 joiners, or a gap between the groups that opened before 2024. [2]
<b>Method:</b> difference-in-differences, defended against a matched comparison and a pump-scheduling simulation. [3]
<b>Checks:</b> reruns from a clean clone within 1%; a verification log; the pumps' summed readings checked against the meters of the feeders that serve only pumps, same hours, after line losses. [4]
<b>Result:</b> 4.6 kW per pump (95% interval 2.9 to 6.3).</p><ol class="lx-ex-static"><li value="1"><b>Proficient:</b> Typed, with an audience (the board), a metric with units (the billing hours' average, not the co-op's single highest hour) and a counterfactual.</li><li value="2"><b>Proficient:</b> The falsification statement: the result that would show the tariff did not cause the fall.</li><li value="3"><b>Proficient:</b> Two alternatives, one from another family (simulation).</li><li value="4"><b>Proficient:</b> A clean-clone rerun, a log and one check against an independent reference (<span class="lx-term" data-term="feeder">feeder</span> meters): of the measurements, not of the tariff's effect.</li></ol></div>
<div class="lx-ex-ans good"><p class="lx-eyebrow">Revised: Strong · Strong</p><p class="lx-ex-lines"><b>Question:</b> the same, and is the fall above 1.5 kW per pump, the least for which the board would keep the tariff? [1]
<b>Method:</b> the same. Limit: the later joiners' demand might still have moved differently. Mitigated: in the four summers before 2024 the two groups moved together, within 0.5 kW a year. [2]
<b>Rerun:</b> a co-op engineer reran the clean clone and got 4.6 kW. [3]
<b>Validation, set up first:</b> summer 2025, not used to build the analysis: the same code on the 29 farms that joined in 2025, against the 42 that never joined. [4]
<b>Rule and result:</b> the check supports the same decision for the 2025 cohort if its whole 95% interval is above 1.5 kW. 2025: 4.1 kW (1.8 to 6.4): it does. [5]
<b>Result:</b> 4.6 kW per pump (95% interval 2.9 to 6.3), above 1.5 kW across the interval.</p><ol class="lx-ex-static"><li value="1"><b>Moves it to Strong:</b> Framing's Strong level: the answer that would change the decision.</li><li value="2"><b>Moves it to Strong:</b> Method fit's Strong level: the method's limit stated and partly mitigated.</li><li value="3"><b>Moves it to Strong:</b> Trustworthy analysis at Strong, first half: reproduced by someone else.</li><li value="4"><b>Moves it to Strong:</b> Second half: data not used to build it, a named comparison group, and a rule written down before looking.</li><li value="5"><b>Moves it to Strong:</b> It supports the decision threshold, not the size of 4.6 kW, and is not proof the effects are equal: the estimates share farms, so no interval for their gap is given. The never-joiners, a new comparison group, need their own case.</li></ol></div>
</div>
<table class="lx-facts lx-ex-diff"><thead><tr><th scope="col"></th><th scope="col">Revised: Proficient</th><th scope="col">Revised: Strong</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Framing</th><td>Typed question, audience, metric with units, counterfactual, what would count against it</td><td>Also the answer that would change the board's vote (1.5 kW)</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Method fit</th><td>Defended against two alternatives</td><td>Also its limit stated and partly mitigated</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Trustworthy analysis</th><td>Clean-clone rerun, log, a meter check against an independent reference</td><td>Rerun by someone else; checked on a summer not used to build it, by a rule set first</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p class="lx-hint">Illustrative: the study is fictional, and its results are assumed example outputs, not computed.</p></div>
<div class="lx-xcard"><header class="lx-x-head"><h3>The rerun, worked</h3></header><dl class="ckr-fields one"><div><dt>Tolerance</dt><dd>1% of the main result, written down before the rerun.</dd></div><div><dt>Values</dt><dd>Reported 4.6 kW; rerun 4.3 kW. Difference: (4.6 − 4.3) ÷ 4.6 = 0.3 ÷ 4.6 = 0.065, or 6.5%: over the tolerance.</dd></div><div><dt>Cause</dt><dd>Three pumps whose meters were replaced mid-summer were removed by hand before the first run; the code kept them. The data note had set that rule before any result.</dd></div><div><dt>Fix</dt><dd>The rule, not agreement with the old number, decides: it is now in the cleaning script, and the rerun from a clean clone gives 4.6 kW.</dd></div><div><dt>Logged</dt><dd>Both numbers, the cause and the fix, in the verification log. Then a co-op engineer reran it from the repository: 4.6 kW.</dd></div></dl></div>
<div class="lx-xcard"><header class="lx-x-head"><h3>The seven marked tasks</h3></header><div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-facts ckr-ans"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Task</th><th scope="col">Answer</th><th scope="col">Why</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">2. The most serious concern</th><td data-l="Answer">b. Each farm chose whether to join, so the joiners may differ from the rest in ways that also change their pumping.</td><td data-l="Why">Joiners chose the tariff, so their demand might have moved differently anyway (<span class="lx-term" data-term="selection-bias">selection bias</span>). Different starting levels alone do no harm; <span class="lx-term" data-term="parallel-trends">parallel trends</span> needs evidence. The other three threaten the causal claim less directly.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">3. Whose peak?</th><td data-l="Answer">a. Framing</td><td data-l="Why">Framing: a metric with units. The co-op is billed for its 20 highest-load summer hours (the billing note), so the pumps' average kW in those <span class="lx-term" data-term="coincident-peak">coincident-peak</span> hours answers the board, not each pump's own peak.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">4. Answering the selection concern</th><td data-l="Answer">c. We now compare the 2024 joiners with the 29 farms that joined in 2025, before they joined, and show both groups' four summers before the tariff.</td><td data-l="Why">Answer with a change and evidence. The 2025 joiners are one possible comparison; their four summers before 2024 test whether the two groups' demand moved alike (<span class="lx-term" data-term="parallel-trends">parallel trends</span>), which matters more than equal starting levels.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">5. From Proficient to Strong</th><td data-l="Answer">b. State the method's main limit here (the later joiners' demand might still have moved differently) and partly mitigate it: show that both groups' peak-hour demand moved together in the four summers before 2024.</td><td data-l="Why">Method fit's Strong level: “limits of the chosen method stated and partly mitigated”. Limit: the later joiners' demand might still have moved differently. Mitigation: the groups moved together, within 0.5 kW a year, before 2024.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">9. A clean-clone rerun</th><td data-l="Answer">1. Clone the repository into a new, empty folder. 2. Build the environment from the repository's lock file. 3. Fetch the raw data with the repository's script, which runs in that environment, and check the checksums. 4. Run the whole pipeline, from raw data to the main result, with one command. 5. Compare the main result with the reported value, against the tolerance written down beforehand. 6. Log the outcome, and any difference with its cause, in the verification log.</td><td data-l="Why">Clone, environment, data, run, compare, log. The download script runs in the environment, so the environment comes first; each step uses only what the repository holds, so a missing file or a hand step shows up.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">10. How far apart?</th><td data-l="Answer">About 6.5%: (4.6 − 4.3) ÷ 4.6 = 0.3 ÷ 4.6 = 0.065</td><td data-l="Why">(4.6 − 4.3) ÷ 4.6 = 0.3 ÷ 4.6 = 0.065, or 6.5% of the reported value: far over the 1% tolerance written down before the rerun.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">11. What to report</th><td data-l="Answer">c. Find the cause, turn any hand step into code with a stated rule, rerun from a clean clone, and log both numbers, the cause and the fix.</td><td data-l="Why">The cause: three pumps with meters replaced mid-summer, removed by hand under a rule the data note set before any result. The rule is now in the cleaning script; the rerun gives 4.6 kW, logged.</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>

</div>
```
